problem: A company monitors incoming emails for spam. On average, $18$ out of every $150$ emails are spam messages. The emails are checked one by one until a spam email is found. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that a spam email is found before checking the $4$th email is{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of emails checked until a spam email is found. On average, the chance that any single email is spam is 

$$
p=\frac{18}{150}=0.12.
$$

So, the number of emails that are checked before finding a spam email can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.12.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.12).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.12)^{x-1}(0.12) \\  & =(0.88)^{x-1}(0.12)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding a spam email before checking $4$ emails is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\in {1,2,3}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(0.88)^{1-1}(0.12)+(0.88)^{2-1}(0.12)+(0.88)^{3-1}(0.12) \\  & =(0.12)+(0.88)(0.12)+(0.88)^{2}(0.12) \\  & =[1+0.88+(0.88)^{2}](0.12) \\  & ≈0.319,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
